Title: Bluegrass & BBQ Silent Auction Dinner
Content: Please join us for the FTCC Foundation Bluegrass & BBQ Silent Auction and Golf Tournament! The Silent Auction will be 6 PM on Thursday, April 27th at the FTCC Tony Rand Center with a $5,000* reverse raffle, live music, B&B catering, and Roland's Dance Studio line-dance lessons. Title: FTCC SGA presents Jazz Flutist Galen Abdur-Razzaq in Concert
Content:
In observance of Black History Month, the Student Government Association and the Student Activities Office presents Jazz Flutist, Galen Abdur-Razzaq in concert with his Jazz ensemble, on Monday, February 27th, 7:00pm-8:30pm in the Tony Rand Student Center.  He is a nationally known Jazz Flute Clinician and one of the most popular college campus entertainers in the country. In addition to the free concert, he will offer a lecture on Jazz and the American Civil Rights movement in Room 9 of the Tony Rand Student Center. Razzaq is a talented and extraordinary flutist from Montclair, New Jersey who has performed both domestically and internationally for over 30 years. A former student of the Berkley College of Music and a graduate of Rutgers University, Razzaq holds a master's degree in Fine Arts and Education. he is an arranger, composer, director, educator, and writer.

Jazz Flutist Galen Abdur-Razzaq in Concert Monday, February 27th 7:00pm - 8:30pm Tony Rand Student Center

Title: African American Heritage Club - Workshop on "Genealogy of the Afro-American Family: How to Get Your Family Tree Started"
Content: Who: African-American Heritage Club What: Workshop on "Genealogy of the Afro-American Family: How to Get Your Family Tree Started" with Presenter Elaine T. Cole When: Tuesday, February 28th @ 11am Where: Advanced Technology Center (ATC) Room 203 Questions? Contact Sharlene Malloy at malloys@faytechcc.edu or 910-678-9827  and Tomica Sobers at sobersto@faytechcc.edu or 910-678-7365 This workshop is a brief introduction to the study of genealogy and family historical research involving the investigation of family ancestors through documentation (such as birth records, marriage licenses, and death certificates) dating as far back in time as possible. Participants will receive information on how and where to start the path towards answers to questions about their own family legacy. Participants will understand why researching African American families is different and often more difficult than researching other nationalities, how to make the research easier through a variety of resources available, and how to use skills (such as knowledge of mathematics, geography, and history) to being and continue the journey towards discovering one's family roots. Handouts will be provided during this workshop. Elaine T. Cole is an FTCC Admissions Counselor who has spent over 15 years conducting family and historical research.

Title: Bunker Brews
Content:
Bunker Brews is a event where veterans, military spouse, and civilians alike can learn more about Bunker Labs, network with fellow veterans, subject matter experts, investors, and thought leaders. Our aim is to create a robust environment for veteran business growth and development.

May 18th at Huske Hardware House, Fayetteville, NC

Fayetteville Tech Community College in partnership with Bunker Labs recently launched the Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurship. This first of its kind program at the community college level is based on EntreDots Six Steps to Success program which has been used to train over 450 entrepreneurs over the past 5 years. The accredited class is designed for service members, veterans and military spouses who want to start main street businesses. Come hear from Dr. David Brand, FTCC Senior VP of Academic and Student Services along with Program Director, Brad Lienhart, about how you can earn college credit and pursue your business dreams.

Keynote speaker will be Mr. Robert Elliot.

Robert Elliott is a NC native multi-generational farmer turned Marine Corps veteran who returned home to become a farmer again. He is a devoted advocate to helping ease the problems found in the veteran and agriculture communities in NC and across the country. Robert helps transitioning veterans find their way into agricultural careers by beginning their own farming ventures. He believes that integrating the two industries will help build the future of agriculture and save veteran's lives by helping them find solace on the farm.

Title: 2017 Youth Entrepreneurship Camp
Content: Budding entrepreneurs will learn valuable, hands-on lessons about starting a successful business... and have fun! During the week, students will participate in a variety of engaging start-up simulation games and activities to personally experience the journey from a great idea to a successful business. For example, each team of students will create a television commercial for their new product or service. Highlighting the week will be each team's "elevator pitch" to a panel of seasoned entrepreneurs. Throughout the week, these judges and other successful entrepreneurs from the community will share their personal experiences, insights and lessons from their own new business journeys. Space is limited to 20 students: Sign up today. Open to rising 6th through rising 9th graders interested in starting or running a business. When: July 31st through Friday, August 4th - 8:30am until 3:00pm Cost: $50 which includes lunch and snacks, plus a camp t-shirt Limited to 20 students. Registration ends July 21st (or when enrollment capacity of 20 students is reached) Call 910-678-8496 or email hillp@faytechcc.edu for an application. SPONSORED BY WELLS FARGO

Title: Potential Health Program Students
Content: The Health Program Application for the FALL 2018 ENTRY will open on NOVEMBER 1, 2017 and remain open through JANUARY 30, 2018. Applicants MUST have the following completed in order to access and complete the Student Health Program Application: 1) Official High School Transcript/GED on file with FTCC Admissions Office (regardless of other degrees earned). 2) Successful completion of all program pre-requisites: BIOLOGY and/or CHEMISTRY; Current proficiency in MATH/READING/ENGLISH via Placement Testing and/or college transfer credit. 3) If applying to the Associate Degree Nursing (A.D.N.) or Dental Hygiene (DH), MUST have a current (no more than 3 year old) TEAS Test Score from www.atitesting.com of 58.7 or higher. **TO APPLY** Log in to your WebAdvisor account and click on "Student Health Program Application". Select your program of choice and click on "Submit". Print or take a picture of the receipt that appears on screen. All notifications after application will be sent via FTCC STUDENT EMAIL. ***If you encounter any errors when trying to access the Student Health Program Application, please contact 9(910) 678-8457 or (910) 678-8252 for assistance.***
